Introduction, Zostrianos Fortified by a Holy Spirit
1. [The glorious book] of the sayings that live forever [that] I, Zos[trianos, wrote ...] and Yolaos as I entered the world for those belonging to my generation and [those] (who will come) after me, the elect who live.
2. The God [of] truth lives in actual truth and understanding and light eternal.
3. When I in my mind forsook my interior bodily darkness, soulish chaos, and gloomy, lustful femaleness about which I was unconcerned, and when I had found the limitlessness of my materiality and rebuked the dead creation inside me, including the sensory divine ruler of the world, I mightily declared completion to those with disparate parts.
4. Even though I had explored their ways for a brief period, inasmuch as inexorable birth bestowed visibility on me, I never felt contented with them.
5. Rather, I was accustomed to separate myself continually from them since, despite my [birth] through procreation, my coming into being had been holy.
6. When I had bettered my sinless soul, I then fortified the [spirit] of reason [inside me] and I [could then wake from] the [gloomy slumber and discover] my [fatherly] God [...].
7. Despite my having [labored on this in every way], I was fortified by a holy Spirit that surpasses even God.
8. [It rested] on me alone while I was bettering myself, and I beheld the Perfect Child, [who he is], and what [he possesses].
9. Frequently and [in varied (forms)] he appeared to me as a willing [oneness] while I was searching for the [male] All-Father, “of [those] things intellectual and sensorial, specific and general, [partial] and entire, encompassing and encompassed, physical and non-physical, spiritual and material,” and [matters] relevant to all of these, and the (state of) existence mixed with them and with the god of this ‹Perfect Child›, the ungenerated Kalyptos, the power [inside] them all.
Zostrianos’ Questions Regarding Existence
1. Regarding existence, given that they originate from the aeon of those who come from an unseen and undivided self-generated spirit in the form of triadic ungenerated images, how can existent beings possess an origin that excels existence and also pre-exist all [of these], yet nevertheless have come to exist in the [world]?
2. How is it that those who are in its presence together with all these [spring from the lofty] Good?
3. What kind [of power] and [source does it possess, and] what place does [it] hold?
4. What is its (originative) principle?
5. How is it that what it produces belongs to it as well as to all of these (others)?
6. Given that [it is a] singular [oneness], how is it self-different, given that it exists in the modes of existence, form, and blessedness and bestows power by being alive in a living way?
7. How has existence that is non-being appeared in a power that possesses being?
8. Searching for the understanding of these questions, according to the tradition of my people, each day I would offer them up to the god of my fathers.
9. I would praise all of them, given that my forefathers and forebears who sought found.
10. Regarding myself, I did not cease looking for a place of repose that my spirit deserved, where I would be unbound in the sensorial world.
The Angel of Knowledge Appears to Zostrianos
1. Then, while I was greatly distressed and depressed on account of the weakmindedness that enfolded me, I had the courage to act and to give myself to cruel death by the wild desert beasts.
2. In front of me stood the angel of the knowledge of light eternal, and he said to me: “Zostrianos, why have you gone insane, as if you were ignorant of the mighty eternal lofty beings?
3. [Are you not aware that you are an elect person], and that you were consequently notified concerning [what you are to do], so that you could now be rescued?
4. Do not ever [be] harmful or [pay heed] to those who are familiar to you so that you do rescue none but those [whom] the Father on high would choose (for rescue).
5. [Do you think] that you are the father of [your people], or that Yolaos is your father?
6. [You have] a godly angel [who has shown] you [the path] by means of saints.
7. Come and surpass these [(lowly) aeons], to which you will return at some other [time] to declare a living [nation] in order to rescue those who deserve it and to strengthen the elect, because the struggle of this age is long, but the time [of] this world is brief.”
Zostrianos Ascends through the Aeons
1. After he had told [me] this, I was very eager and happy to embark with him on a large shining cloud, and I [departed from] the shape of my molded body on the earth, protected by glories.
2. [We] fled the entire world and the thirteen aeons therein, together with their angelic host.
3. We were not seen, but their chief was upset by [our journey], because [our] shining cloud, whose [essence] excelled [the entire world], was indescribable.
4. Its beauty glowed intensely.
5. It has a power to [guide] pure spirits, because it is a life-giving spirit and an intelligible mind, [un]like worldly entities [constructed] of malleable matter and swayable reason.
6. I realized then that my inward strength had conquered the darkness, because it consisted entirely of light.
The Baptisms of Zostrianos
1. I was baptized there, even receiving the image of the glories, and I was transformed into one like them.
2. I journeyed through the atmosphere of the [earth], even passing by the aeonic simulacra after baptizing myself seven times [there in] living [water], once for each [of the] aeons.
3. I did not stop before [I had passed] simultaneously [through] all of them.
4. I ascended to the sojourn that [truly] exists.
5. [I] was baptized, and [I forsook the world].
6. I ascended to the repentance that truly exists, [and] there [I was] baptized [six] times.
7. I journeyed through the sixth one [and I was strengthened by the same].
8. I ascended to the [self-generated] aeons, and there I stood after seeing a true light that truly exists.
9. It existed truly from its self-generated root, [together with] tall angels and glories [beyond] stature.
10. I was baptized [by] those powers that oversee [the] living water, Michar and Mi[cheus].
11. I was baptized in the [name of] the divine Self-Generated One.
12. I was cleansed by the mighty Barpharanges.
13. I was [glorified] and inscribed in glory.
14. I was sealed by those who oversee these powers, [Michar], Micheus, Seldao, Ele[nos], and Zogenethlos.
15. I [became] a [contemplating] angel and stood together with the souls on the first aeon, which is the fourth.
16. I blessed “the divine Self-Generated One and the forefather Pigeradamas, [(who is) an eye of] the Self-Generated One, the perfect Primal [Human], and Seth Emm[acha Seth], the son of [A]damas, the [father of] the [unshakeable race], and the [Four] Lights, [Armozel and Oroiael, Daveithe and Eleleth], and Mirothea, the mother [of Adamas], and Prophania, [the mother] of the lights, and Ple[sithea], the [mother of the angels].”
17. I was [baptized the] second time by these same powers in the name of God, the Self- Generated One.
18. I was transformed into a masculine angel.
19. I stood on the second aeon, which is the third one, together with the children of Seth, and I blessed these same ones.
20. And I was baptized for the third time by these same powers in the name of God, the Self- Generated One.
21. [I] was transformed into a holy angel and stood upon the third [aeon], which is the second one, and [blessed] these same ones.
22. And I was baptized for the fourth time by these [same] powers.
23. I was transformed into a perfect [angel and stood on] the fourth aeon, [which is the first] aeon, and [I blessed these same ones].
Zostianos’ Questions Regarding Singularity and Duality
1. I then looked for [a single power among them].
2. I spoke [these words]: “I [...] of [...].”
3. And I [asked] him [about how to understand them]: “In light of the variations of human hearing, why [are there variations] in the ability [to hear] them?
4. [Are these same things] their abilities, or are they the same things, just with varying names?
5. Does one soul differ from another soul?
6. Why do human beings differ from each another?
7. In what mode and to what degree are they human?”
8. The mighty primacy, Authrounios, said to me: “Do you ask about those things through which you have journeyed?
9. Or why this atmosphere of the earth exhibits this worldly model?
10. Or how many aeonic simulacra there are?
11. Or why they are [un]moved?
12. Or about the sojourn and repentance, and about the [aeonic] creation and the world that [does not really exist?
13. I will teach] you [plainly] about [all these things you ask] me.
14. [No revelation] or [commandment] will be visible to you, not [even from the] Unseen [Spirit, until after you understand these things], and the [teaching that ... Eleleth ... that] will become apparent to you.”
15. [And we two joined with the aeons through] which I had [journeyed].
Authrounios Describes the Creation
1. And the [mighty] primacy, Authrounios, said [to me]: “The atmosphere of the earth came into being through a principle of reason, and in an imperishable mode it manifests things generated and perishable for the sake of the coming of the mighty judges.
2. This is (so that they do not experience sensory) perception and become confined in the creation.
3. When they, however, encountered it and by this perceived the works of the world, they sentenced its ruler to a perishability that typifies the world, because that gloomy, perishable [production] is an [essence] and principle of matter.
4. When Sophia gazed [downward], she beheld darkness, [illuminating it] while she retained [her own station], being a paradigm for [worldly] things, [a principle] for the essence [without essence and the] form [without] form [...] a shape [without shape].
5. [It accommodates every worldly entity ...] the All [... the perishable production, because it is a principle of reason that sways] the darkness.
6. [He sows from his] reason, because [the ruler] of [creation] can[not] see any of the eternal entities.
7. He beheld a reflection, and from a reflection that he [beheld] in (the reflection), he created the world.
8. Using a reflection of a reflection, he moved on the world, and then even the reflection of (the reflection that) had appeared (to him) was taken away from him.
9. Sophia, however, was granted a place of repose that rectified her repentance.
10. The result was that because no pure, original image dwelt inside her, neither pre-existing inside him, nor previously coming to be through him, he exercised his imagination and formed what remained, since the image Sophia possesses is ever perishable and deceitful.
11. The archon, however, looked downward, [because he simulates] and incorporates by means of [chasing after the image] owing to the overflow [that tended downward].”
12. When [I heard and] saw these [things, I could comprehend] the mind of [these who concentrated their mind] on the things they do not [understand].
13. Because he has concentrated [his mind on ... the] aeons [...] mightier than [...]
14. And [again he said: “Sophia became] perfect by [the will of the leader] through whom [the atmosphere of the earth endures], having [unchangeably averted] the destruction of the world.
15. Now the aeonic simulacra exist in the following manner:
16. They have failed to obtain an equally powerful form, [instead] possessing eternal glories, and they exist as judgment seats for each of the powers.
17. When souls, however, are illuminated by the light inside these simulacra, and by the model that frequently develops [effortlessly] inside them, then the soul believes that she witnesses [the truth] and the eternal [source inside] the blessed [idea that exists] as the only singularity. [...] each of [...] light that [...] all, and she [...] entirely, and she and a [...].
18. And she [...] she who [...] she [...] of [the sojourn, and the evidence] for the repentance [dwells with the souls] in accord with the power [inside them, so that] they could stand.
19. And inferior [souls] are prepared by the aeonic simulacra, which receive a simulacrum of their souls while they still dwell in the world.
20. After the aeons emerge one by one, they come into being and one by one are conveyed from the simulacrum of the sojourn to the sojourn that truly exists, from the simulacrum of the repentance to the repentance that truly exists, [and from the] simulacrum of the self-generated aeons [to the self-generated aeons] that truly exist, and so on [...].
21. The souls [...] exist inside a [light ...] them all [by means of the] aeonic [simulacra].
22. [On the one hand, they] see, [but whenever ...] and certain [...] out [...] the [...] outside [...] light [...] of [... all] those [who] are [... as they] [bless] “[the God] over the [mighty] aeons, and the [ungenerated] Kalyptos, the mighty male Protophanes, the Perfect [Child] who is more exalted than God, and his eye, Pigeradamas.”
Zostrianos Asks Ephesech About the Waters
1. I invoked the Child of the Child Ephesech.
2. He stood in front of me and said: “O messenger of God, Child of the Father, [you are] the Perfect Human.
3. [Why] do you invoke me and ask concerning the things you know, as if you were [unaware] of them?”
4. [I, however, said]: “I ask concerning the water, [how then does] it bestow perfection and convey [its power]?
5. What are [its] powers?
6. [Are they the names] in which we are baptized?
7. [Why do] these names [differ from those], and why [do the waters differ] from each [other?
8. And are they whole] in the [... from] others [...] humans [...]?
9. [Why do they differ in this way from each other]?”
10. [The Child of the Child Ephesech, the Savior, answered]: “[Zost]trianos, listen concerning [all] these matters!
11. The number of the pre-[existent] principles is three, despite their appearance from a unitary principle [of] the aeon Barbelo.
12. This is not an indeterminate number of principles and powers, nor are they productions of any arbitrary source and power.
13. To the contrary, “they have brought every principle into manifestation and have granted power to every power, and have appeared in what by far excels them, these being existence, blessedness, and life.”
14. [These have appeared] with each [other and they have appeared] from a [unique singularity], and so [...] they were named [on account of their] greater [glory ... unique ...] and [certain ...] a perfect [...] from [a unique principle, and it is] a [unitary singularity ...] ever [...].
15. And [there exists] a water for [each one] of them.
16. They are consequently [three] perfect waters.
“17. It is the water of life that pertains to life, in which now you have been baptized in the Self-Generated One.
18. It is the [water] of blessedness that [pertains] to understanding, in which you will be [baptized] in the Protophanes.
19. It is the water of existence [that] pertains to divinity, that is, to Kalyptos.
20. And the water of life [exists with regard to] power, that of [blessedness] with regard to essence, and that of [divinity] with regard to [existence].”
21. All [these], however, [are likenesses and forms of the] Triple-Powered One.
22. They are the ones that [flow from the] pure water [... they] are also [the model ... water] in accord with ... [as they] depart ... [male ... there ...] existence [as it] is.
23. [They] not only [dwelt] in thought, but he [accommodated] them, because he is [(the power of) becoming] in the following manner.
24. He enforced a [limit] on being, so that it would not become infinite and formless.
25. Becoming was instead truly delimited while it was still but a new entity so that [it] could become an entity possessing a proper [dwelling], existence and [being] together, standing together with it, existing together with it, enclosing it, [and being like it] in every aspect.
26. [It departed] from the [living water so that it could] obtain the [pre]-existent [firmness] of [...] action [...] visible [...] and his word [...] these after [...] they became [... accommodating] for a [...].
27. And the power exists together with essence and existence of being, whereas this water exists, and the name in which one is baptized is a spoken utterance of this water.
Kalyptos and the Path of Ascent
1. Consequently, the first perfect water of the Triple-Powered One, ‹that of› the Self- Generated One, [is] life for perfect souls, because it is a mental utterance pertaining to the coming into being of both the perfect [mind and of] that [(other) one].
2. This is because the source of all [those] is the Unseen Spirit, whereas the others originate [from understanding], given that they are his likenesses.
3. He who, [however], simultaneously knows [in what mode he exists] and what [the living water is, one like that] lives by [understanding.
4. What pertains to understanding] is the [water of life], and in [becoming, life] becomes [infinite, so that it can attain to] its [own (proper) being ... and] the name [...].
5. [...] he truly exists; this is the case because he limits himself.
6. They [draw near to] this water in accord with this equality of power and position.
7. The mighty male, the unseen Perfect Mind Protophanes possesses his own water, as you [will see] when you reach his dwelling.
8. The ungenerated Kalyptos also (possesses his own water).
9. Regarding each one there exists an incomplete and [preliminary] form, so that in this way they might reach completion.
10. The self-generated aeons comprise four completed occurrences of the all-perfect ones [that pre-exist] the [perfect individual ones].
11. And the [fifth] aeon [encompasses] the [divine] Self-Generated One, because [they] all [originate from the perfect, divine triple]-male [Child], because [they are] entireties [...], perfect [divine ... the triple-male ... the perfect] individual ones [...] in the [...] [19] perfect, those who exist in species, genus, complete, and partial differentiation.
12. In the same way, the path of ascent that surpasses what is perfect ‹is› with Kalyptos.
13. The divine Self-Generated One is the chief ruler over his own aeons and angels, being portions of him, because those who one by one comprise the four, at the same time they comprise the fifth aeon, while the fifth exists in oneness.
14. Considered one by one, the four [comprise] the fifth, but all of these are complete as individuals [because they] possess a [single principle].
15. In this way [the triple-male] is also a [perfect individual], because he is a [power] of the divine [Self-Generated One].
16. And the unseen [perfect] male mind [Protophanes is the dwelling-place] for those who [exist in harmony among the aeons].
17. A [... resembling] living and perfect portions.
18. Regarding the All, even the all-perfect race and that which surpasses the perfect and blessed:
19. The self-generated Kalyptos is a pre-existent origin of the Self-Generated One, being God and Forefather, a source of Protophanes, a Father of his own portions.
20. Being a fatherly God, he is foreknown, but not known.
21. As he is a self-originated power, so is he self-fathered, so that he is without father.
22. The unseen Triple-Powered One, who is all [of their] forethought and the Unseen Spirit, he is [the origin of all of them] and [an existence without substance prior to essence] and existence [and being.
23. Existents precede] life, [because it is] the [source of] blessed[ness.
24. And ...] the [stature ...] all [these the ...] [exist] among them.
25. [They descended] among the others, yet they [are all] commingled in several places, any place that is attractive and pleasant.
26. They exist everywhere and they exist nowhere.
27. They encompass spirit, since they are bodiless, yet they surpass bodiless entities.
28. They are undivided, possessing, together with those who are purer than they, living thoughts and the power of truth, because in this regard their spiritual purity is greater and does not resemble bodies that exist in only one place.
29. Most importantly, there is no compulsion in them, not in whole and not in part, so that their path of ascent is pure, [since it is imperishable].
30. Each one [of their powers has] designated [for itself] its own [root].
31. And [...] them [...] its own proper aeons, so [he] then [knows] how to obtain an eternal model.
32. And the world intellect enters in, joining when the water of the Self-Generated One is completed.
33. When someone knows both this and all of these, that one is dealing with the water of Protophanes.
34. When someone joins with him and with all of these, that one is dealing with Kalyptos.
35. Among the aeons a similar situation prevails.
36. With respect to knowing these one by one along with their portions, they are [perfect].
37. Those who belong to the All, where knowledge dwells, and what they know, have [become separate], but they do share something in common with each other.
38. The All and all [of these possess the] baptism in the [baptism of the Self-Generated One].
39. If the [...] perfect [...].
40. The one who demonstrates that he has reached knowledge of how he belongs to him and feels a shared communion has washed in the baptism of Protophanes.
“41. And if someone understands their source, how all of them are manifested in but one principle, and how all who are joined become separated, and how those who were separated rejoin with each other again, and how the portions [join together with] the entireties and the species with the [genera],” when someone has understood these matters, they have washed in the baptism of Kalyptos.
42. For each place, one possesses a portion of the eternal ones, and ascends [to them.
43. Just as] someone [becomes pure and] single, in this way they incessantly [draw near to] unity.
44. Being [ever] pure and [singular], one is filled [with mentation], with existence [and spirit], even a holy Spirit.
45. Nothing of him exists outside of him.
46. On the one hand, he [beholds] “with a perfect psyche those who belong to the self-generated ones; with intellect those of the triple-male; with a holy Spirit, those who belong to the Protophanic ones.”
47. On the other hand, he hears concerning Kalyptos by the powers of the Spirit from whom they have emerged in a far more excellent revelation of the Unseen Spirit.
48. And through the thought that presently exists in silence, even within the First Thought, he hears concerning the triple-powered Unseen Spirit.
49. Furthermore, it is a hearing and a silent power cleansed with the perfect life-giving Spirit, the [primary] perfect and the all-perfect one.
50. There are, consequently, glories assigned as [nurturers] to them.
51. Those who in truth have been baptized in knowledge and those who are deserving are protected, but those who [do] not belong to this category [are ordinary entities], and they [will revert back] to [their original root.
52. One who originates from] the fifth is [contended with those belonging to the aeonic] simulacra.
53. [Each] of the aeons [has] a baptism [of this kind] assigned to it.
54. Should [someone] strip themselves of the world and put aside [nature], if someone is a homeless and powerless sojourner who acts as others do, or if someone sinless repents, being contented with knowledge, and is not worried about anything pertaining to the world, baptisms are assigned for each of these respectively:
55. First is the path (leading) to the self-generated ones, the (path) in which on each occasion you have been baptized, being proper for beholding the [perfect] ones.
56. It is a universal knowledge that originated from the powers of the self-generated ones.
57. Then follows the (second) baptism you are to conduct when you relocate to the all-perfect aeons.
58. The third baptism, after washing in it, you will [then] hear concerning those [that exist] in truth in [that] place.
59. Next, regarding [these] names, they resemble the following:
60. There exists a singularity, [even a singular genus], resembling [perfected things] on account of their [coming into being amidst] existing things, and [they have come into being because] a mental utterance of them exists, [and because] there is a name that exists in truth, [as] they do.
61. On the one hand, existents subsist in an idea that resembles them, even its generic resemblance that is its natural quality.
62. On the other hand, one sees, knows, arrives, and becomes like his genus through auditory speech and hearing.
63. By hearing alone, however, they remain powerless, being sensorial and physical, so that they only appropriate things insofar as they can receive them.
64. This is a [distant] image of the sensorial or rational category, and although it excels material nature, it is lower than intellectual essence.
Differences Between Souls
1. Wonder not at the differences between souls.
2. When someone believes that they are different (from other souls), they consequently do [not] (believe they are) similar (to them), despite their [participation] in things that [perdure (in existence)].
3. [Next], if someone [appears] with a [soul] and then [utterly] perishes, then their [souls have become disin]carnate.
4. Someone else [who exists during] his (life)time, and [(continues) existing] for a period (of time), their soul has become [in]carnate.
5. Next, those who have utterly [perished] are (of) four (categories), while those [(existing) within] time are (of) nine, each possessing its (own proper) quality and tendency.
6. Despite their being similar, they are nevertheless different.
7. Despite their individual distinctiveness, they are nevertheless at least stable.
8. And other immortal souls join together with all of these souls on account of Sophia who gazed downward, because there are three species of immortal souls:
9. Those who have sent down roots in sojourn possess no self-generated power.
10. (Instead), they follow the ways (generated by) others (who are) a single [self-contained] species.
11. Second are those who stand [on] repentance.
12. They [were not undecided about] transgression, because knowledge sufficed [for] them, (but) because they are neophytes, [they still sin].
13. This category, nevertheless, also possesses differentiations.
14. Some of [these] have sinned, (while) others [also] have repented, and yet others [merely plan to repent].
15. Consequently, there are [three] categories of these latter ones:
16. Those who have committed every sin, but have repented, those who have sinned in part, and those who planned to sin, (but did not).
17. For this reason, their aeons are even six, in accord with the place reached by each one of their souls.
18. The third category belongs to the souls of the self-generated ones, possessing an indescribable but knowable, rational narration of the truth, in addition to self-generated [power] and eternal [life.
19. And] they possess four differentiations in the same mode:
20. Angelic forms, those who love truth, those who hope, and those who are faithful.
21. [In fact], they [also] have [consorts], and they dwell [inside them as four places of] the self-generated ones:
22. [The first] is that of [perfect life].
23. The [second] is [that of mentation].
24. The [third is that of eternal] knowledge.
25. The fourth is that which [pertains to] deathless [souls].
The Four Lights and the Ascent of the Soul
1. The Four Lights dwell [there] in the same mode:
2. [Arm]ozel [is assigned] to the first aeon, (being) a longing for God and truth, one who joins souls (together).
3. Oroiael, a seer of truth, is assigned to the second.
4. Daveithe, a seeing of knowledge, is assigned to the third.
5. Eleleth, a fervent desire and eagerness for truth, is assigned to the fourth.
6. The four exist as intellectual utterances of truth and knowledge.
7. They exist, despite their not belonging to Protophanes, but to the Mother.
8. A thought of the perfectly illuminated mind causes deathless souls to attain knowledge.
9. [He who is sufficient] for them is [the God] Arse[n]oas, the Self-Generated One, a revelation [from the power] of all of them, [because] he is an [intelligible], unspeakable mental utterance [of the] truth who [proclaims plainly] concerning the [Perfect Mind], which is that it is a loftier [principle inseparably] [united] in a communion between itself and an [intelligible] light and thought inside its own (proper) aeon.
10. Even Adam is the [Perfect] Human, an eye of the Self-Generated One.
11. His knowledge ‹is aware› of the divine Self-Generated One as a mental utterance of the truthful Perfect Mind.
12. The son of Adam, Seth, approaches each soul as sufficient knowledge for them, which is why the [seed] of life originated from him.
13. Mirothea is [she in whom] the divine Self-Generated One [appeared] together with [Adamas].
14. She is a thought of the Perfect Mind pertaining to her own existence, to what she is, to [how] she existed in the past, and to how she exists in the present.
15. God, the Self-Generated One, therefore, is a mental principle and is knowledge, a knowledge [that originates from a mental power].
16. Congruent with this, [the soul of] Adamas [is singular, being the power] of the [singular ones to whom] it appeared.
17. [It is a] transfiguration of souls.
18. It is also [a power of the] Perfect [Mind].
19. For the sake of [those who are perfect and] the angelic host [it has frequently appeared].
20. Consequently, [if the cosmic] soul [exists that makes them and pre-exists even the sensorial world], the aeonic simulacra [that] in truth [exist, and the sojourn] that [in truth exists, and] repentance, [(these) are the ascent] to this place, up [to the self-generated] aeons that exist [in truth].
21. Should [the soul discover] and love [the truth], she will stand on [the fourth] aeon, [obtaining] Eleleth the light, [which will] become a meditative [thought].
22. [And if] it hopes and senses, it will become a [masculine] gendered [angel] that has stood on [the third, obtaining Daveithe the light].
23. [If] it is united [to the truth, it will then] stand [on the] first [aeon, obtaining] Ar[mozel the light].
